newsitem.title: USA: G7 to discuss emerging markets, Africa, corruption.
newsitem.headline: G7 to discuss emerging markets, Africa, corruption.

text.p: The Group of Seven is expected to discuss on Sunday steps to strengthen emerging market financial systems, fight corruption and help Africa, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Friday.
"Promoting reform ... to transform more developing countries into dynamic emerging markets is clearly in the interest of the United States," Rubin told reporters.

Finance ministers and central bank chief from the G7 -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States will gather on Sunday on the fringes of the semi-annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
"We are moving toward consensus on a strategy to strengthen emerging market financial systems," Rubin said. "This is critically important to reduce the risks of future financial crises."

That strategy includes agreement on a set of core guidelines and principles as well as specific recommendations for international financial institutions and regulators on how to help emerging market economies implement them.
The United States is also pushing for a broad international initiative to fight corruption worldwide, Rubin said.
The Treasury chief urged industrial nation governments to act quickly eliminate the tax deductibility of bribes of foreign officials and to make such bribery against the law.
"We also urge the IMF and the multilateral development banks to expand the scope of their activities in the anti-corruption area," Rubin said.
He said the G7 will also discuss on Sunday ways to help African nations.
"We in the United States and Africa's other main trading partners should focus on trade and investment, while U.S. support should respond to those countries doing most to help themeselves," he said.
